chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad) from Safwan from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman who performs Hajj without a Wali (guardian). He said: 'There is no harm (in it), even if she has a husband or a brother or a son of a brother, and they refuse to perform Hajj with her, and they do not have the means (to go), so it is not fitting for her to stay away from Hajj, and it is not for them to prevent her.'

And he said: 'The divorced woman does not perform Hajj during her waiting period (Iddah).' And the woman whose husband has died, during her waiting period, there is no harm in her going out to perform Hajj, but it is not for the divorced woman to do so. Narrated.

key_terms.الْمُعْتَدَّةُ: The woman in her waiting period
key_terms.عِدَّتِهَا: Her waiting period after divorce or death
key_terms.وَلِيٍّ: Guardian or male relative accompanying the woman

ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform Hajj alone if her husband or male relatives refuse to go with her?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the conditions under which a woman may perform Hajj independently, emphasizing that the refusal of male guardians to accompany her does not obligate her to remain behind if they lack the means. The text further delineates the status of waiting periods (*Iddah*), permitting widows to travel for Hajj while restricting divorced women, reflecting the distinct legal implications of death versus divorce in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the balance between the obligation of Hajj and the practical constraints of family guardianship (*Wilayah*).
